byCritic.checked: Full read of all 11 files in lib/src/core plus all 9 test files and the reference-python oracle. Ran `npm test` (252 pass). Regenerated fixtures via `python3 gen_fixtures.py` — no drift. Cross-language parity beyond the fixtures: 300 fresh random constraint scenarios, `validate` agreed on all 300, and on the 255 feasible ones `constrainedGreedy` was byte-identical to `constrained_gen.constrained_greedy` on edge list, degree sequence, ASPL, diameter and connectivity. Fuzzed constrainedGreedy hard guarantees (prohibited absent, required present, degree cap, legal-edge maximality, determinism) over 4000 random feasible constraint sets — clean. Verified `girth` against a brute-force shortest-cycle oracle over 6000 random graphs and confirmed edge-insertion-order invariance for girth/shortestPath/eccentricity/allPairsSummary; confirmed buildConstrainedBuddyGraph, polishConstrained and polish are invariant to both reversed constraint insertion and reversed edge insertion over 400 cases. Traced that forceConnect's Set-order-dependent component walk is genuinely inert (completion exits legal-edge-maximal; step count is bounded well below the completionCap). Verified buildConstrainedBuddyGraph never throws over ~2000 malformed (n,k,options) combinations including priorHard, and traced the arithmetic showing checkPolishSize cannot throw out of either builder even with explicit `polish: true`. Confirmed MAX_REPAIR_WORK does not fire on the largest greedy-admitted shapes ((1000,12),(2000,3),(5000,2),(1200,5)). Swept buildBuddyGraph over n=2..22 x k=2..6 recomputing every returned metric from the returned edges (aspl, diameter, connected, girth, largestComponentFraction, buddies, regular, degreeMax<=k, asplGap>=0) — all agree, all deterministic. Checked n=0/1/2, k=0/1, k>=n, mind demotion floor against gen_c_cached, n!=cons.n, everyone-under-degree, one-vs-many components. Verified ringGreedy's in-place incremental distance-cache update is exact despite reading partially-updated rows (single-edge min-plus identity is a fixed point, so it agrees with the numpy copy-based reference).

Full-surface adversarial DoS/robustness pass over lib/src (all 11 modules + lib/test), measured against the shipped lib/dist build, probes under .review-scratch/.

GATE ORDERING (cost before commitment): traced every cap against the work it bounds. validateDetailed orders structuralReasons -> MAX_CONSTRAINED_N -> k-validity -> MAX_CONSTRAINED_WORK -> degree vectors -> O(n^2) connectivityReasons; the expensive walk is last (measured 68 ms at the n=5000 ceiling). checkPolishSize precedes input.copy() and energy() in polish, and precedes the copy/sweeps in polishConstrained. ringGreedy's MAX_CACHED_N and MAX_GREEDY_WORK both precede ring(n) and the Int32Array(n*n) allocation. refusedResult clamps to MAX_CONSTRAINED_N not MAX_ROSTER.

BUDGET HONESTY (re-measured rather than trusting the comments): constrained (5000,4) 16.2s, (464,463) 48.3s, (550,330) 38.3s, (600,277) 34.8s, (1000,100) 25.8s, (2000,25) 22.3s, (465,464) refused. Unconstrained (1000,12) 38.5s, (2154,3) 20.5s, (1709,4) 22.2s, (5000,2) 1.9s. All inside the documented ~46s/~60s envelopes. Polish: measured the realised unit rate of MAX_POLISH_WORK at n=120/500/1000/2000/5000 -> flat 4.5-5.4e7 units/s, so the 8.65e8 budget caps polish at ~19s at every n; the "calibrated at one point in (n,k) space" hypothesis is dead.

UNMODELLED TERM: greedyWork charges nothing for minSeparation, and findPair pays a full O(n^2) eccentricity scan per demotion (up to floor(n/2) times). Bounded above by n^3/2 vs greedyWork's 1.5n^3 at k=3, and the ecc loop is skipped entirely at k=2. Measured (2154,3) 20.5 -> 24.0s with minSeparation 1077; (1000,12) 38.5 -> 35.3s. Not exploitable.

NUMERIC EDGES: swept [-1, -0, 0, 1, 2.5, NaN, +/-Infinity, 5e9, 1e21, 2**53, "3", null, undefined, {}, []] through n, k, seed, polishIters, priorWeight, minSeparation on both builders and mooreLowerBounds. No hang, no native RangeError, no NaN in a result. polishIters is genuinely reduce-only after round 15 (clamped to the caller's own fallback, 20000/8000), so retiring MAX_POLISH_ITERS left the ceiling intact by construction on both paths. priorWeight null/undefined correctly take ?? DEFAULT_PRIOR_WEIGHT; non-finite/negative/non-number normalise to 0 and report priorsKeptFraction null.

THROW-VS-REFUSE: tried to make buildConstrainedBuddyGraph throw. checkPolishSize is the only candidate and cannot fire: max n(n+m) = n^2(1+k/2) subject to n^2*k <= 1e8 and n <= 5000 peaks at 7.5e7, against a 2.25e8 fixed charge of an 8.65e8 budget leaving 6.4e8 for a 7.5e7 iteration. Same for buildBuddyGraph + polish:true (peak 5e7 at (5000,2)).

DETERMINISM: 80 paired builds with the same required (then prohibited) pair set inserted in reversed order, auto-polish active. Zero divergence — Set insertion order reaches nothing observable (choosePartner sorts on farness/degree/index, edgeList canonicalises, forceConnect is provably inert because completion exits only at legal-edge maximality).

BUILD-ARTIFACT SKEW: lib/tsconfig targets ES2020, so #checkEndpoints/#prohibited downlevel to __classPrivateFieldGet brand checks on the hottest read path (~n^2*k/2 hasEdge calls). Suspected the budgets were calibrated on vitest's modern transform. Rebuilt at ES2022 and compared: 2308 vs 2582 ms, 3776 vs 4275 ms, 12.1 vs 12.2 s — ~10%, within calibration margin.

SPREADSHEET/CLIPBOARD SINK: not present in this component. lib has no CSV, clipboard, filename or DOM surface, and formatReason interpolates only numbers. That lens belongs to app/.

Constraints.fromTags still has no caller outside lib/test (grepped app/src, lib/src, scripts), so its O(n^2) materialization remains correctly filed as a deferral in lib/CLAUDE.md; not re-filed as noise.

Baseline: lib suite green, 252 tests / 9 files.

Full-surface read of lib/src/core (graph.ts, budgets.ts, constraints.ts, greedy.ts, constrainedGreedy.ts, polish.ts, swap.ts, metrics.ts, bounds.ts, rng.ts, index.ts) and lib/CLAUDE.md's own known-limitations ledger, cross-referenced against docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md and app/CLAUDE.md to identify the actually-committed next change.

Two concrete extension attempts against real files, not speculation:

1. Declared OCP seam (constraints.ts TagPolicy switch in Constraints.fromTags): added a second live case ("require_same", mirroring prohibit_same but calling c.require instead of c.prohibit) directly in src/core/constraints.ts, ran `npm run typecheck` and the full `npm test` suite (252 tests) with no other file touched. Both passed clean. The change was then reverted (git diff empty). This confirms the seam genuinely pays exactly as lib/CLAUDE.md claims: validateDetailed, buildReport, connectivityReasons, degreeOf etc. are already generic over required/prohibited/prior pairs, so a new policy branch needs no caller changes.

2. F11 (construction replay) — the one place PROJECT_PLAN.md explicitly states core work is required ("F11 is therefore core work first... not a UI concern only") — traced what implementing a construction trace/bestAtIter would actually require: ringGreedy (order is implicit in the loop, cheap), repairDegrees (mutates in place, void return, no result object to extend), constrainedGreedy (three separate mutating phases — required edges, extendOne loop, forceConnect — with no trace channel), polish (PolishResult would gain bestAtIter, correctly identified in lib/CLAUDE.md as sitting exactly at `best = g.copy()`), polishConstrained (returns a bare Graph today, no result type at all — the biggest gap), swap.ts (Swap already carries enough detail to reconstruct trace deltas, no change needed there), and index.ts (BuddyResult/ConstrainedBuddyResult would need new fields to carry the trace to callers). Confirmed by grep that no caller (app or test) references fromTags, priorHard, or any replay/trace concept today. This fan-out is real but is already documented accurately in lib/CLAUDE.md's known-limitations section as a deferred item with the correct reasoning (no caller in the tree yet), so I am not re-filing it — re-filing an already-correctly-deferred item would just be duplicate bookkeeping, not a new finding.

Also checked: legalEdge/constrainedMeasure remain factory functions rather than caller-injectable predicates (consistent with the stated determinism/hard-constraint rationale, not rigidity); the tag-policy switch has only one live case today but is a single trivial switch arm plus a throwing default, not a class hierarchy or DI container, so it does not read as gratuitous machinery for a single variant; index.ts's size (~590 lines) is a facade over two builder entry points plus their shared helpers (summarize, buildReport, refusedResult, resolveWantPolish/autoPolishEnabled, withHardPriors, degreeExtent) — each helper has one clear responsibility and none reach toward UI concerns, so it reads as a composition root doing facade work, not a god component; metrics.ts/bounds.ts/rng.ts/swap.ts are each single-purpose with swap.ts a genuine (not speculative) shared dependency of both polish.ts and constrainedGreedy.ts today.

themes.theme: Optimization pass result fields (`polished`, `priorsKeptFraction`) are derived from the decision to invoke the pass rather than from what the pass actually did, so a zero-iteration run is misreported as a completed/measured pass
findingSummaries: `polished` is set from the decision to CALL polish rather than from anything polish did, so a pass that executes zero iterations is reported as polished — and `priorsKeptFraction` is then published as a measurement when nothing ever weighed the priors.
themes.remediation: Delete the call-site-derived `polished`/`priorsKeptFraction` assignments and drive both directly off the pass's own executed-iteration count (`iters`) in every builder that sets them, so there is a single source of truth instead of separate inferred values per call site.

themes.theme: A comment about `minSeparation` overstates the field's inertness ("nothing reads it") when the code in fact reads and forwards the value, just without acting on it
findingSummaries: Comment states 'nothing reads the field' for minSeparation, contradicted by lines 348 and 376-377 where the field is accessed and passed through.
themes.remediation: Remove the inaccurate 'nothing reads the field' clause from the comment rather than adding new qualifying language, leaving only a factual note that the value is unused once forwarded.

gating.theme: a result field asserts that an optimisation pass ran when the pass performed zero iterations, so the caller cannot tell a measured number from a coincidental one
gating.summary: `polished` is set from the decision to CALL polish rather than from anything polish did, so a pass that executes zero iterations is reported as polished — and `priorsKeptFraction` is then published as a measurement when nothing ever weighed the priors.
gating.failure: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(60, 4, cons, { polishIters: 0 })` (cons carrying 30 priors from a previous round) returns an edge list BYTE-IDENTICAL to `{ polish: false }`, but reports `polished: true` and `report.priorsKeptFraction: 0.0333…`; the same call with `{ polish: false }` correctly reports `polished: false, priorsKeptFraction: null`, and with polish actually running reports 1.0. `boundedPolishIterations` honours 0 (it is an integer >= 0), so `polishConstrained` returns its input untouched. Reachable with NO option at all whenever the graph has fewer than 2 edges: `buildConstrainedBuddyGraph(12, 0, cons)` -> `polished: true, priorsKeptFraction: 0`. Same on the unconstrained builder: `buildBuddyGraph(30, 4, { polishIters: 0 })` -> `polished: true` on a graph identical to `{ polish: false }`. This is the open sibling of the correction already recorded at lib/src/core/polish.ts:87 ("loopIters 0, no accept/reject decision, the input returned byte-for-byte, and `polished: true` reported. A silent no-op sold as work"), which closed only the anneal-calibration route into the same state.
gating.remediation: Make the fact flow from the pass instead of from the call site: have `polishConstrained` report the iteration count it actually executed (as `polish` already does via `PolishResult.iters`), and in BOTH builders set `polished = iters > 0` and gate `priorsKeptFraction` on `active.priorHard || (iters > 0 && priorWeight !== 0)`. Fixing only the `polishIters: 0` case leaves the `m < 2` case (k<=1 rosters) open, and fixing only the constrained builder leaves `buildBuddyGraph` open — both are the same fact being inferred rather than observed.
gating.invariant: For every input to either builder, `result.polished === true` implies the polish pass executed at least one accept/reject decision (equivalently, `polished === false` whenever the pass's effective iteration budget is 0 or the graph it was handed has fewer than 2 edges); and `report.priorsKeptFraction === null` whenever priors were not promoted to required and no polish iteration was executed.

gating.theme: Comment claims field is never read, but code reads and passes it through
gating.summary: Comment states 'nothing reads the field' for minSeparation, contradicted by lines 348 and 376-377 where the field is accessed and passed through
gating.failure: Claim: 'nothing reads the field' (line 228). Reality: options.minSeparation is accessed at line 348 and passed to constrainedGreedy. Further contradiction at line 376-377 which explicitly states 'minSeparation is passed through to constrainedGreedy'.
gating.remediation: Replace 'nothing reads the field' with 'nothing USES the field' or 'the field is read but ultimately ignored' to accurately reflect that the value is accessed but not acted upon.
gating.invariant: The prose describing field usage must match reality: if a field appears on the right-hand side of an assignment (accessed/read), the comment must not claim it is never read
